property_summary: After a caller successfully calls withdrawAll, the caller's recorded credit in the contract must be zero (credit[msg.sender] == 0); the mutant that clears credit before the external call can cause an observable difference in contract balance behavior when the callee re-enters, breaking this invariant for some inputs.

For any caller and deposit amount, after withdrawAll returns the contract balance decreases by exactly the withdrawn amount (address(c).balance == initialBalance - amount); the mutant that zeroes credit before the external call can allow reentrant behavior to change final balance, breaking this rule for some inputs.

For any depositor and deposit amount, if withdrawAll() is called by an attacker contract that REENTERS during the external transfer, the reference contract C (which clears the caller's credit only after the external call) will always revert on reentrancy because of its reentrancy lock, so the call either succeeds once and leaves credit==0 and address(c).balance decreased by the withdrawn amount, whereas the mutant that moves credit clearing before the external call can allow reentrant re-entry to observe a different final contract balance; this test asserts that after a single withdrawAll() attempt by a reentrant attacker, the reference leaves the contract balance equal to initialBalance - withdrawnAmount (i.e. exactly one withdrawal happened) for all fuzzed inputs, which the mutant violates for some inputs.

For any depositor and deposit amount where the depositor is an EOA (non-contract), calling withdrawAll always results in the depositor's recorded credit being zero afterwards (credit[depositor] == 0); the mutant that moves the credit-clearing line earlier can cause a contract-call reentrancy or different observable behavior only when the callee is a contract, but for EOAs the reference always leaves credit == 0 while the mutant can differ for some inputs involving contract callers — we therefore fuzz the caller type and amount and constrain to EOAs so the reference satisfies the rule for all admissible inputs while the mutant fails for some inputs when the caller is a contract (the test asserts credit == 0 for EOAs and thus will pass on reference and be violated by the mutant for some fuzzed inputs).

For any caller address and deposit amount where the caller is a contract that reverts during the external payout, the correct contract C preserves the invariant that withdrawAll() call itself returns (does not revert) while the buggy mutant can cause withdrawAll() to revert for some inputs because it zeroes credit before the external call; thus the rule: when a depositor that is a reverting contract calls withdrawAll(), the reference C's withdrawAll() never reverts for any admissible inputs, while the mutant can revert for some inputs.
